evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》; graphic inventory
evidence.text: The dictionary analyzes 候 as 从人、矦聲, with the early sense ‘watch/keep lookout, reconnoitre’. It reports a received 《說文》 definition and cites 《呂氏春秋·貴因》: 武王使人候殷. Its character page lists one small-seal and four bamboo/slip forms, but no oracle-bone or bronze forms for 候. These are source statements; the available page does not establish the date or manuscript witness of each slip form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「候」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry transmits the 《說文》 analysis ‘伺望也。从人，矦聲’ (Daxu edition) and Duan’s ‘司望也。从人，侯聲’. It says the seal form was written from 人 and 侯, and describes the later regular-script shape as having the human-side portion of 侯 reduced to a short vertical stroke. It dates no specific transition. Listed senses include reconnoitre, watchtower (通堠), visit, wait, serve, and divination; the entry supplies classical citations, including 《呂氏春秋》 for reconnoitring and Tao Yuanming’s 晋-period ‘僮僕歡迎，稚子候門’ for waiting.
evidence.title: A00191 候 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 侯 entry: 形義通解; 《說文》; 《廣韻》
evidence.text: The related character page says oracle-bone and bronze forms of 侯 are analyzed as 厂 plus 矢, depicting arrows gathered at a target (箭耙), with target as the proposed original sense; it also reports oracle-bone use for noble rank and bronze use for lords and personal names. It transmits the 《說文》 explanation of the target and records 《廣韻》 戸鉤 for 侯. The target depiction is the dictionary’s analysis, not independently established here; the page does not give the pronunciation of a target’s name in the early period.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「侯」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 侯 entry: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: For 侯, the dictionary says its regular form is conventionally written 侯, while its graph should be analyzed/normalized as 矦 and assigned originally to the 矢 section; later common writing changed it and classified it under 人. This supports treating 矦 in 候 as a form related to 侯, but does not by itself prove a chronological ancestry between the exact spellings 矦 and 侯. The same page cites 《說文》’s target account and distinguishes target, noble-title, and other lexical uses.
evidence.title: A00150 侯 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The page classifies 候 as a phono-semantic compound: semantic 亻 plus phonetic 矦, giving Zhengzhang Old Chinese *ɡoːs for 候 and *ɡoː for 矦; it describes the 矦 shape in the graph as modified. This is a modern secondary account. A separate source, the MOE dictionary, gives Mandarin hòu for 候 and hóu for 侯, while the HK dictionary reports 《廣韻》 戸鉤 for 侯 and 候’s 《說文》 胡遘切. These readings support a historical sound relationship, though their tone distinction and differing modern tones show that the graphs are not homophones in modern Mandarin.
evidence.title: 候 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: 漢字ペディア, Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation
evidence.field: なりたち; readings and meanings
evidence.text: This Japanese character dictionary calls 候 会意形声, describes 人 plus a changed-form 矦 (コウ), and says ‘侯の後にできた字’ (‘a character made after 侯’). It lists modern Japanese on-reading コウ, and senses including observing, waiting, serving, sign/omen, season, and the honorific auxiliary そうろう. This is a dictionary’s graphic account, not a dated paleographic sequence. Its claim that 候 was made after 侯 is compatible with a derived graph but does not determine whether 矦 is a full positional form or a historical ancestor of 侯.
evidence.title: 候 | 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア

evidence.text: The displayed passage reads ‘武王使人候殷，反報岐周曰：「殷其亂矣。」’ It is a textual attestation of 候 used for observing/reconnoitring. The page search result identifies a 四部叢刊初編 base text; an open attempt returned 403, so the full source page could not be inspected in this session.

gaps: No dated physical inscription or manuscript image for 候 was visually inspected. The HK character page reports no oracle-bone or bronze examples and supplies only undated small-seal and bamboo/slip graphic listings.

The available evidence supports a phonetic relationship between 候 and 侯/矦, but does not establish a direct chronology between the spelling 矦 and 侯. The MOE description of normalized 矦 and later conventional 侯 is related-character evidence, not an explicit genealogy for the component in 候. For that component relation, use uncertain unless the project’s component-form convention treats 矦 as a full positional counterpart.

The proposed original referent of 侯 as a target is a dictionary paleographic analysis. No independently recovered early name or pronunciation for the depicted target was found; do not claim borrowing of a target’s name as the explanation for 候’s sound.

The dates and source witnesses for the received Shuowen forms and the dictionary’s bamboo/slip exemplars were not established. Search result snippets are not used as proof of a physical object’s date.

The 《呂氏春秋》 reconnoitring passage is textually cited by multiple dictionary records and returned in search, but direct inspection of the Ctext page failed with 403. Its textual layer/date was not independently dated in this research.

The semantic sequence from watch/reconnoitre to wait, visit, serve, omen, and season is not fully demonstrated as a chronological chain. Dictionary citations support separate uses, including reconnoitring in 《呂氏春秋》, waiting in the 晋-period Tao Yuanming citation, and other later senses; the sequence connecting them remains an analysis, not a chronology inferred from gloss order.

The phonetic comparison is documented with modern Mandarin hòu (候) and hóu (侯), reconstructed Zhengzhang Old Chinese *ɡoːs and *ɡoː from a secondary source, and received Guangyun fanqie evidence. A character-specific result from the Academia Sinica historical-sound database was not retrieved, so no additional reconstruction-system comparison is claimed.
No visual inspection of glyph pixels was performed, and no character-specific 候 glyph image with checked identity and reuse provenance was found; the historical_glyphs list is empty.

The database query and rights pages for Xiaoxuetang could not be opened. Its help document establishes that the database contains sourced representative forms generally, not that any particular queried candidate belongs to 候.
No independently recovered early name or pronunciation for the proposed target depicted by 侯 was found. Do not explain 候’s phonetic value as borrowing the name of that object.

The dictionaries support 候’s sound component as 矦/侯 and the association with 侯; the exact relationship between the spelling 矦 and 侯 within 候 is not dated or genealogically established by the inspected sources.
The Zhengzhang Old Chinese forms are from a secondary source. No character-specific reconstruction from Xiaoxuetang or another inspected reconstruction system was retrieved in this pass.

The dictionary’s examples support distinct senses or uses, but do not establish a dated semantic pathway from reconnoitring to waiting, visiting, service, omen, or season. No chronology is inferred from gloss ordering.

No directly inspected dated manuscript or inscription containing 候 was obtained. The received dictionary citations to classical works do not by themselves establish the date of the surviving witness or first physical attestation.
